premises.text: Circling for parking is a major urban traffic problem
premises.evidence_span: half of the traffic in Brooklyn is actually caused by people circling for a parking spot

premises.text: Strangers can find and reserve each other's curb spots through a smartphone social network
premises.evidence_span: these two have never met. But with Curve Karma, Marissa can find and reserve Heather's parking spot

premises.text: Karma Credits ($1) fund reservations and split value between giver and platform
premises.evidence_span: When Heather gives her spot to Marissa, she earns one of those Karma credits worth a dollar, and she can use that Karma credit next time she is looking for parking. The other Karma credit goes to Kirp Karma

premises.text: Map publishing, need-a-spot matching, private messaging, GPS nav, and mutual rating constitute the handoff product
premises.evidence_span: And Marissa can use the built-in navigation feature using GPS to navigate to the spot

premises.text: High-demand spots turn over frequently; the platform takes one credit per exchange as revenue
premises.evidence_span: And because Curb Karma earns a Karma credit for every exchange, we make $400,000 a year in revenue

premises.text: Parking pain is global, supporting multi-city expansion
premises.evidence_span: parking's actually a problem all over the world

value.text: Awesome parking found where and when needed via the network
value.evidence_span: Marissa scored an awesome parking spot

causal_links.evidence_span: But what's in it for Heather? Well, Heather can earn something called a Karma Credit
end that madness and to disrupt parking
Curb Karma finds you parking where and when you need it

notes: Optional dependency: credits are presented as what makes leavers participate in matching. ASR spellings (Curve/Kirp/Kerb) left in evidence spans.
